```{r}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Path to the Excel file (adjust this to your file's location)
file_path <- "./ThermoDataSummary.xlsx"

# Reading the Excel file
df <- read_excel(file_path)
print(head(df))

# Renaming the first column to "Model" if it's not already named
if ("...1" %in% colnames(df)) {
  colnames(df)[1] <- "Model"
}

# Melting the data frame from wide to long format using pivot_longer
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -Model, names_to = "ModelName", values_to = "Percentage") %>%
  mutate(Type = rep(c("% of metabolites", "% of reactions"), each = n()/2),
         Percentage = as.numeric(as.character(Percentage)),
         Percentage = ifelse(Type == "% of metabolites", -Percentage, Percentage))

print(head(df_long))

top_models <- df_long %>% group_by(ModelName) %>% summarise(Total = sum(Percentage)) %>% top_n(20) %>% pull(ModelName)
df_filtered <- df_long %>% filter(ModelName %in% top_models)


p <- ggplot(df_filtered, aes(x = ModelName, y = Percentage, fill = Type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "identity", width = 0.7) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-100, 100)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = abs, breaks = seq(-100, 100, by = 20)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "black", linewidth = 1.5) +
  labs(title = "Percentage of thermocuration in GEMs",
        y = "% of Total",x=NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 35) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 40, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 35),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 45, face = "bold", hjust = 5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 28, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 32),
    axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(t = 0, r = 10, b = 0, l = 10)),
    axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.25, linetype = 'solid', colour = "grey85"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(linewidth = 0.15, linetype = 'solid', colour = "grey90")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("% of metabolites" = "#56B4E9", "% of reactions" = "#D55E00"), name = "Type", labels = c("Metabolites", "Reactions"))

# Printing the plot
print(p)

```
